research.domain: Implementation of per-expert hot/warm/cold tiering on a stock-GGUF llama.cpp stack: placement granularity, activation-trace capture, eviction + cross-layer prefetch, and recalibration cadence

findings.name: llama.cpp fuses a layer's experts into ONE tensor — -ot is per-layer, never per-expert
findings.claim: In stock llama.cpp, all experts of a MoE layer's FFN projection are stored in a single fused 3D tensor (blk.N.ffn_{gate,up,down}_exps.weight, shape {n_embd, n_ff, n_expert}); --override-tensor/-ot regex-matches WHOLE tensor names to buffer types, so its finest static-placement grain is per-layer-per-projection — an individual expert cannot be statically placed.
findings.detail: GLM-4.6 converts to blk.91.ffn_gate_exps.weight of shape {5120, 1536, 160} — all 160 experts stacked in one tensor. PR #11397 (slaren) implements -ot as a std::regex over the full tensor name (e.g. '[2-9][0-9]\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU' keeps layers 20-99's experts on CPU) mapping matches to a buffer type (CPU/CUDA0). It operates on entire named tensors, not sub-tensor/per-expert slices. This is the single most load-bearing finding for the per-expert lane: it kills static per-expert placement on this engine.
findings.design_implication: The planner's STATIC placement schema must emit tensor-name globs (per-layer-per-projection), NOT expert indices. True per-expert tiering is impossible as an -ot plan; it must be a RUNTIME cache (see per-expert-cache-is-the-runtime-hook).
findings.metric: GLM-4.6 ffn_gate_exps {5120,1536,160} = 160 experts in 1 tensor; -ot matches whole tensor names

sources.title: llama : add option to override model tensor buffers (PR #11397)
sources.claim: -ot/--override-tensor maps a tensor-NAME regex to a buffer type (CPU, CUDA0...), operating on entire named tensors only; example '[2-9][0-9]\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU'.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle (WebFetch) confirmed: author @slaren, title verbatim, regex example present, and explicitly 'operates on entire named tensors, not individual expert slices within tensors.'

sources.title: Insufficient documentation for -ot and --override-tensor flag (Discussion #13154)
sources.claim: -ot targets per-layer tensor TYPES (routed _exps vs shared _shexp, gate/up/down) but cannot subdivide the routed-expert block into individual experts.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle confirmed shared-vs-routed splitting via tensor names (blk.2.ffn_gate_exps vs blk.2.ffn_gate_shexp). The fetch summary's headline 'individual experts CAN be targeted' is a type-vs-index conflation — the quoted evidence is expert TYPES, not indices; the gating claim stands on the fused-tensor layout (#11397 + #20757).

sources.title: convert_hf_to_gguf.py — GGUF MoE expert tensor layout
sources.claim: Expert weights convert to a single 3D tensor per FFN projection per layer; the third dimension is the expert count (e.g. 160), not N separate named tensors.
sources.verifier_note: Corroborated by #20757's byte-offset addressing into one fused CPU tensor; both LLM lenses rated the fused-tensor claim PLAUSIBLE.

findings.name: Per-expert tiering must be a RUNTIME cache at llama.cpp's #20757 hook point
findings.claim: The only per-expert behavior in stock llama.cpp is a runtime copy of the ACTIVE experts' sub-rows by byte offset (expert_offset = first_id * expert_size) CPU->GPU, with NO slot remapping or cross-pass persistence — so per-expert hot/warm/cold tiering must be built as a persistent GPU-slot cache ABOVE this copy.
findings.detail: Issue #20757 quotes the exact hook: 'it copies by byte offset into a GPU tensor that mirrors the full CPU tensor layout (expert_offset = first_id * expert_size, line 1529)' and 'no slot remapping, no persistence across passes. This is the hook point for the cache.' The issue PROPOSES exactly what gpu-container's per-expert lane needs: a GPU buffer of N slots (--moe-expert-cache-size N, N << n_expert), a persistent expert_id->slot_idx map carried across passes, and pluggable eviction (LRU/SLRU/LFU/FIFO). Its PoC reports 12-14 tok/s steady-state vs 0.5-1 tok/s CPU-only offload.
findings.design_implication: gpu-container's per-expert tiering is NOVEL vs all stock engines. Phase-2 build target: either implement the runtime expert-slot cache (the #20757 layer, with Least-Stale eviction) or contribute to/ride that upstream effort. The cache — not -ot — is where hot/warm/cold per-expert placement lives.
findings.metric: #20757 PoC: 12-14 tok/s steady-state vs 0.5-1 tok/s CPU-only offload

sources.title: Feature Request: Two-tier GPU+RAM expert cache for MoE offload (pluggable eviction policy) (Issue #20757)
sources.claim: Active experts are sub-rows of one fused CPU tensor copied by byte offset to a GPU mirror with no slot remapping or persistence; the issue proposes --moe-expert-cache-size N + expert_id->slot map + selectable eviction; PoC 12-14 tok/s vs 0.5-1.
sources.quant: 12-14 tok/s vs 0.5-1 tok/s; expert_offset = first_id * expert_size (line 1529)
sources.verifier_note: Oracle (WebFetch) confirmed all three points VERBATIM, including the 'no slot remapping, no persistence... hook point for the cache' quote and the --moe-expert-cache-size N proposal with LRU/SLRU/LFU/FIFO.

sources.title: Loads of interesting ideas in the 'ktransformers' report (Discussion #8721)
sources.claim: KTransformers / ik_llama.cpp also tier routed experts at expert-group/tensor granularity (hot in VRAM, rest in DRAM), not arbitrary per-expert device assignment — finer-than-layer placement is a custom-cache problem, not a flag.
sources.verifier_note: Existence confirmed; used to establish that NO off-the-shelf engine offers per-expert static placement, so gpu-container's runtime cache is a genuine contribution. Not independently deep-verified beyond existence.

findings.name: -ot DOES cleanly pin shared/attention to VRAM and route experts to CPU/RAM (the hot tier is expressible today)
findings.claim: Although intra-routed-expert split is impossible, -ot CAN cheaply pin shared experts + attention + router/norms to VRAM and place routed _exps tensors on CPU/RAM per layer — so the 'shared/attention always hot in VRAM' tier is expressible with a one-line flag today.
findings.detail: A regex like 'blk\.\d+\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU' routes the routed-expert tensors to CPU while shared experts (_shexp), attention (attn_*), and norms stay on the default GPU device. This validates the hot-VRAM tier of the architecture (shared/attention/router) without any custom code; only the routed-expert SUB-tiering needs the runtime cache.
findings.design_implication: The planner emits the shared/attention-in-VRAM tier directly as -ot today (low-risk, shipping). Only the routed-expert hot/warm/cold split is deferred to the runtime cache (#20757 layer).
findings.metric: regex 'blk\.\d+\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU' keeps routed experts on CPU; _shexp/attn stay GPU

sources.title: Insufficient documentation for -ot and --override-tensor flag (Discussion #13154)
sources.claim: -ot can split routed (_exps) vs shared (_shexp) experts and target them independently across layers (a Scout MoE layer exposes ffn_{gate,up,down}_exps + 3 _shexp tensors).
sources.verifier_note: Oracle confirmed shared-vs-routed splitting is possible via tensor-type names (the part of #13154 that IS solid); the intra-routed-block split is what's blocked.

findings.name: --n-cpu-moe is per-layer and CPU-COMPUTES offloaded experts (cost model = CPU-compute at decode, PCIe at prefill)
findings.claim: --n-cpu-moe N places experts at per-layer granularity; CPU-assigned experts are COMPUTED on CPU during decode (KTransformers-style), so the offload cost at decode is CPU-compute-bound, while GPU experts stream over PCIe only at batch >= GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH (~32) during prompt processing.
findings.detail: The decode-time bottleneck for offloaded experts is CPU matmul throughput + RAM bandwidth, NOT PCIe; PCIe streaming only kicks in for large batches (prompt processing) above the offload-min-batch threshold (mainline default 32 tokens; ik_llama scales it as 32 * total_experts / active_experts). This is the two-regime cost model the planner must encode.
findings.design_implication: The planner's per-tier cost model must distinguish CPU-compute (decode, offloaded experts -> uses the measured cpu_bw probe) from PCIe-stream (prefill, batch>=32). Conflating them mis-predicts decode tok/s. (Partly already in the Milestone-2/3 cpu_bw input.)
findings.metric: GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH default 32 tokens; decode = CPU-compute bound, prefill = PCIe bound

sources.title: Performant local MoE CPU inference with GPU acceleration in llama.cpp (MoE offload guide)
sources.claim: --n-cpu-moe N keeps N layers' experts on GPU and the rest on CPU (whole-layer unit); CPU experts run on CPU at decode; bulk PCIe copy only at batch >= GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH (default 32).
sources.verifier_note: Non-primary (technical blog), explicitly marked. The CPU-compute-at-decode fact is independently in tensor-engine-knowledge (wave-1/2, verified) and consistent with #20757; both LLM lenses rated the claim PLAUSIBLE. Treated as supporting, not sole-source.

findings.name: No built-in per-expert trace — capture via eval-callback on the top-k/argsort routing tensor -> L×E histogram
findings.claim: llama.cpp has no built-in per-expert activation-trace export; the routing decision is an internal top-k/argsort `ids` tensor (global expert IDs). The lowest-friction capture is the eval-callback (ggml_backend_sched_set_eval_callback / cb_eval), filtering on the routing node and returning false on all other nodes (to avoid forcing host copies), accumulating a per-layer x per-expert (L×E) count matrix — a small offline harness, no fork.
findings.detail: Expert selection is built from ggml_top_k (internally ggml_argsort) producing the per-token top-n_expert_used id tensor with GLOBAL expert IDs (so the histogram maps directly to physical tiers, no remapping). The eval-callback fires per graph node with name+data during llama_decode; returning false on non-routing nodes keeps it a sub-1% probe (MoE-Infinity's EAM overhead budget). The exact routing-node ->name is a one-grep task in build_moe_ffn (src/llama-graph.cpp).
findings.design_implication: gpu-container ships a calibration harness using cb_eval to emit the L×E activation matrix; budget <1% overhead; store the L×E integer matrix (KBs) in the receipt — NOT per-token logs. This is the concrete INPUT that makes 'adaptive calibration' real on llama.cpp.
findings.metric: trace = L×E integer matrix (KBs); MoE-Infinity EAM <1% overhead budget

sources.title: Two-tier GPU+RAM expert cache for MoE offload (Issue #20757) — the routing ids tensor
sources.claim: The selected-expert routing decision exists at runtime as an internal `ids` tensor consumed by the scheduler's expert-copy loop; no logging/callback surfaces it to users out of the box.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle-confirmed (same page as the cache hook). The ids tensor is the capture target.

sources.title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache
sources.authors: Leyang Xue, Yao Fu, Zhan Lu, Luo Mai, Mahesh Marina
sources.claim: An Expert Activation Matrix (L×E counts) is the canonical trace format, populated by intercepting router outputs at <1% overhead.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle: title + authors (Leyang XUE et al., not 'Xie') + 3.1-16.7x + sparsity-aware cache CONFIRMED in abstract; the EAM/<1%/'<5% experts' specifics are in the full paper body (abstract is silent), consistent with wave-1's prior PARTIAL.

findings.name: Turnkey trace alternatives: SGLang ExpertDistributionRecorder + vLLM --enable-eplb
findings.claim: If llama.cpp instrumentation is too costly, SGLang ships an ExpertDistributionRecorder (per-layer physical-expert selection counts for EPLB) and vLLM's --enable-eplb records expert load over a rolling window (default 1000 engine steps) — both produce the L×E table directly.
findings.detail: SGLang PR #4957 ('Expert distribution recording without overhead for EPLB', author fzyzcjy) adds the recorder; Agent-sourced docs give the '--expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat' aggregate mode. vLLM's --enable-eplb (--eplb-config window_size=1000, step_interval=3000, log_balancedness) collects per-forward-pass load. The trace engine need not be the serving engine.
findings.design_implication: A cross-engine calibration path: run a representative trace through SGLang/vLLM to get the L×E table, then apply the per-layer/per-expert plan to a llama.cpp serve. Secondary to the in-llama.cpp eval-callback path (we are llama.cpp-first).
findings.metric: vLLM eplb window_size default 1000 steps; SGLang recorder 'without overhead' (PR claim)

'Without overhead' is the PR's own claim, not an independently measured number.

sources.claim: --enable-eplb collects load statistics every forward pass over a rolling window (--eplb-config window_size default 1000, step_interval 3000) and can log balancedness (avg/max tokens per expert).

findings.name: Least-Stale eviction: stale/current queue partition, evict stale first (key = stale-flag + layer-index)
findings.claim: SpecMD's Least-Stale partitions the expert cache into 'stale' (touched in a prior forward pass) vs 'current' (this pass) and evicts stale first, exploiting the deterministic front-to-back layer order so soon-needed experts are protected; the key is (stale-flag, layer-index) updated per forward-pass (not per token), and it needs no model changes (forward hooks on a stock MoE).
findings.detail: Staleness is a binary flag flipped per forward pass, backed by FIFO/priority structures ordered by layer position (O(log N) insert / O(1) evict), purely retrospective (no future-selection oracle). It beats LRU because MoE expert access follows layer order, not temporal recency — LRU keeps a just-finished early-layer expert while evicting an upcoming one.
findings.design_implication: The runtime expert cache (per-expert-cache-is-the-runtime-hook) uses Least-Stale, NOT LRU/ARC, for the expert slots; key on (stale-flag, layer-index). (LRU/ARC remain correct for KV-cache spill — wrong for experts.)
findings.metric: 2.6-8.6x fewer collision misses typical; up to 85x best-case (abstract); >88% hit at ~5% cache; up to 34.7% TTFT reduction

sources.title: SpecMD: A Comprehensive Study On Speculative Expert Prefetching
sources.authors: Duc Hoang, Ajay Jaiswal, Mohammad Samragh, Minsik Cho (Apple)
sources.claim: Least-Stale eviction exploits MoE's predictable (layer-ordered) expert access; reduces collision misses up to 85x over LRU (2.6-8.6x in per-config measurements) and achieves >88% hit with up to 34.7% TTFT reduction.
sources.quant: up to 85x (abstract); 2.6-8.6x per-config; >88% hit at ~5% cache; 34.7% TTFT reduction
sources.verifier_note: Oracle: paper EXISTS (Hoang/Jaiswal/Samragh/Cho, Apple, 2026), abstract states 'up to 85x over LRU' + '>88% hit' + '34.7% TTFT' VERBATIM. Both LLM lenses independently flagged '85x' as headline-exaggerated -> reframed to lead with the conservative 2.6-8.6x per-config range; the 85x is the real abstract maximum, kept as 'best-case'.

findings.name: Cross-layer-gate prefetch works on STOCK models (run layer i+1's existing router on layer i's state early)
findings.claim: The dominant stock-model prefetch is the cross-layer gate (Fate): run the NEXT layer's EXISTING router on the current layer's hidden state one step early (adjacent layers >83% cosine-similar) to predict its experts — ~99% hit rate, zero new parameters, no retraining. AdapMoE independently corroborates (~90% accuracy, 1.35x speedup, unmodified model).
findings.detail: Fate clones layer i's gate input to predict layer i+1's experts via the native router (no added params, no training), tested on Qwen1.5-MoE / DeepSeekMoE; it pins shallow layers (0-3) fully because they predict worst, spreading the rest of the VRAM budget across deep layers (depth-aware tiering). AdapMoE applies layer i+1's gate to layer i's activations for ~90% accuracy with no finetuning (only an OPTIONAL first-layer predictor needs training).
findings.design_implication: Warm-tier prefetch is realizable on stock GGUFs by invoking layer i+1's router on layer i's residual — no model surgery. Make the hot/warm tiering DEPTH-AWARE: pin the first ~3-4 MoE layers hot, prefetch deep layers via the cross-layer gate.
findings.metric: Fate 99.08% hit / 97.15% prefetch accuracy; AdapMoE 1.35x speedup; >83% adjacent-layer cosine similarity

sources.title: Fate: Fast Edge Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Cross-Layer Gate
sources.claim: Cross-layer gate predicts the next layer's experts from the current layer's gate input (adjacent layers highly similar), raising expert hit rate to ~99% with no additional training; shallow-favoring cache pins layers 0-3.
sources.quant: 99.08% hit / 97.15% accuracy; >83% cosine; shallow pin L=3
sources.verifier_note: Oracle: first author Fang, 2025, abstract confirms cross-layer-gate + 'increases the expert hit rate to 99%' + adjacent-layer reuse. The 97.15%/83% sub-numbers and shallow-pin are body-level (Agent retrieved the html). mistral's lone CONTRADICTORY ('needs retraining') is the known LLM blind spot — overridden by the abstract + AdapMoE.

sources.title: AdapMoE: Adaptive Sensitivity-based Expert Gating and Management for Efficient MoE Inference
sources.claim: Applies the next layer's existing gate to the current activations (~90% accuracy) on an unmodified model for 1.35x speedup with no accuracy loss; only an optional first-layer predictor needs training.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle: first author Zhong, 2024, '1.35x speedup without accuracy degradation' CONFIRMED in abstract; the 'unmodified model / no finetuning' detail is body-level (abstract silent). Corroborates Fate's stock-model conclusion (which is the firmer source). Repo PKU-SEC-Lab/AdapMoE is a reference impl.

findings.name: SCOPE EXCLUSION: Pre-gated needs a fine-tuned model (out); MoE-Beyond needs a trained predictor (deferred)
findings.claim: Not all prefetch methods work on stock GGUFs: Pre-gated MoE REQUIRES changing the architecture and fine-tuning the pre-gates ('incrementally trained during the fine-tuning stage') -> OUT OF SCOPE for stock-GGUF gpu-container; MoE-Beyond keeps the base model stock but needs a separately TRAINED transformer predictor (66M traces) -> a build-and-own deliverable, only if cross-layer-gate (free) proves insufficient.
findings.detail: Pre-gated's body states verbatim 'change the MoE model architecture to properly accommodate... our pre-gate function' and 'our pre-gate functions are incrementally trained during the fine-tuning stage' — so a stock Mixtral/Qwen GGUF cannot use it as-is. MoE-Beyond trains a lightweight transformer predictor (multi-label sequence prediction, 97.5% acc / 86.6% F1) on activation traces; the MoE is unmodified but the predictor is a per-model offline training step.
findings.design_implication: v1 uses cross-layer-gate prefetch (stock, free). EXCLUDE Pre-gated (we cannot ship a fine-tuned model). MoE-Beyond is a DEFERRED option (own a trained predictor) gated on Fate-style prefetch proving insufficient on target GGUFs.
findings.metric: Pre-gated 81% of GPU-only (needs fine-tune); MoE-Beyond 17%->72% hit at 10% budget (needs trained predictor)

sources.title: Pre-gated MoE: An Algorithm-System Co-Design for Fast and Scalable Mixture-of-Expert Inference
sources.claim: Pre-gated MoE changes the model architecture and incrementally trains the pre-gate functions during fine-tuning — it requires a modified, fine-tuned model, not a stock pretrained one.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle (body fetch): VERBATIM 'change the MoE model architecture' and 'pre-gate functions are incrementally trained during the fine-tuning stage'. Year corrected 2024->2023 (arXiv 2308; ISCA'24 venue). This is the load-bearing scope-exclusion, firmly verified.

sources.title: MoE-Beyond: Learning-Based Expert Activation Prediction on Edge Devices
sources.claim: Base MoE is unmodified, but a separately-trained lightweight transformer predictor (on 66M expert-activation traces) lifts GPU cache hit from 17% to 72% at a 10%-of-experts budget.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle: first author Gavhane, 2025, abstract FULLY supports — 'base MoE is unmodified', 'lightweight transformer model', '17% to 72% when only 10% of experts fit'. Cleanest verification in the wave.

findings.name: Recalibrate on DRIFT, not a timer: streaming change-detector tripwire + divergence confirmation
findings.claim: Because expert skew is request-level and aggregates to uniform, a static histogram is valid only for its trace; recalibration should be DRIFT-gated: a cheap always-on streaming change detector on the warm-tier miss-rate (ADWIN, parameter-free, significance delta=0.002; or DDM, 2-sigma warning / 3-sigma alarm) as the tripwire, confirmed by a distribution signal (JS divergence / chi-square between the calibrated vs EWMA-decayed live expert histogram).
findings.detail: ADWIN keeps a variable-length window, splits it, and declares drift when sub-window means differ beyond a bound at delta=0.002, then drops the stale half (the kept window IS the fresh calibration sample). DDM treats each warm-tier miss as Bernoulli and uses 2-sigma/3-sigma control limits to separate transient load spikes (warning -> start buffering a candidate trace) from real drift (alarm -> commit the re-trace). A JS/chi-square divergence between calibrated and live expert distributions confirms the CAUSE is routing shift, not transient load.
findings.design_implication: The routing half of gpu-container's recalibration loop fires a re-trace only on a CONFIRMED drift step-change (miss-rate detector + histogram divergence), never per-request or on a fixed timer. This closes the per-expert loop without constant re-tracing cost.

sources.title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache
sources.claim: Per-request expert activation is highly skewed but aggregates toward uniform across diverse requests, so any offline histogram is valid only for the trace it was cut from.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle-verified (Leyang Xue et al., 2024); the request-level-skew-aggregates-to-uniform premise is the reason cadence must be drift-gated.

sources.title: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing (ADWIN)
sources.claim: ADWIN is a parameter-free streaming change detector that auto-sizes its window and flags drift at significance delta (default 0.002) with bounded error rates.
sources.verifier_note: Canonical drift detector (Bifet & Gavalda, SIAM SDM 2007). River-docs page retrieved by the research agent; both LLM lenses rated the drift-gating claim PLAUSIBLE.

sources.title: Learning with Drift Detection (DDM)
sources.claim: DDM monitors a binary error/miss stream via statistical process control: 2-sigma warning, 3-sigma drift alarm; samples between form the new training set.
sources.verifier_note: Canonical concept-drift detector (Gama et al., SBIA 2004). Cited by name/attribution from the research agent; not individually re-fetched by the oracle this run (well-established, low fabrication risk, both LLM lenses PLAUSIBLE). DOI may resolve via Springer.

findings.name: Between re-traces, continuously self-tune the warm/cold split (EWMA/hyperbolic heat; ARC ghost lists; LeCaR)
findings.claim: Between expensive re-traces, keep tiers tracking gradual drift for free: maintain each expert's tier priority as an EWMA/time-decayed ('hyperbolic') heat score updated per-iteration, and self-tune the warm/cold boundary with ARC-style ghost lists (a burst of ghost-hits on just-demoted experts = mis-sized split) or LeCaR regret-minimization (best when cache << working set — our exact case).
findings.detail: Hyperbolic caching gives O(1) frequency-with-aging (priority = access-count / age) that self-adjusts to shifting popularity. ARC keeps ghost lists of recently-evicted keys and shifts the recency/frequency target by ghost hits (0.75% overhead, 10-20% over LRU). LeCaR models eviction as online learning over {recency, frequency} via regret on wrongful evictions, winning most when the cache is far smaller than the working set — which is exactly the VRAM-warm-tier-vs-full-expert-set situation.
findings.design_implication: Continuous cheap update (EWMA heat + ghost-list split-tuning) absorbs GRADUAL drift, so the costly re-trace only fires on a confirmed STEP-change (drift-gated-recalibration-cadence). A rising ghost-hit / wrongful-eviction rate is itself a cheap drift signal.
findings.metric: ARC 0.75% overhead, 10-20% over LRU; Hyperbolic 10-20% lower miss; LeCaR up to 18x on small caches

sources.title: ARC: A Self-Tuning, Low Overhead Replacement Cache
sources.claim: ARC self-tunes the recency/frequency split online using ghost lists of evicted keys, matching offline-tuned policies at 0.75% space overhead.
sources.verifier_note: Oracle (WebSearch, USENIX page 403'd to direct fetch): CONFIRMED Megiddo & Modha, FAST '03 (2003), ghost lists, self-tuning recency/frequency, 0.75% overhead, 10-20% over LRU.

findings.name: Cadence mirrors tiered JIT: cheap always-on counters, expensive recompile on threshold, anti-thrash guard
findings.claim: The 'when to recompute an adaptive policy' problem is solved in tiered JIT compilers (HotSpot): cheap always-on hotness counters, expensive recompilation triggered only at a threshold, with a deopt-counter guard against recompile thrashing — mapping directly to per-iteration hit-rate/divergence counters (cheap) -> re-trace on threshold (expensive) -> a 're-trace within N tokens' guard against recalibration thrashing.
findings.detail: HotSpot increments invocation/back-edge counters in low tiers; crossing Tier3/Tier4 thresholds triggers C1/C2 recompilation, and deopt+recompile is rate-limited so pathological code doesn't recompile forever. The structural lesson (two-level: always-on cheap profiling + threshold-gated expensive recompute + anti-thrash guard) is domain-general.
findings.design_implication: Adopt the two-level structure with an EXPLICIT anti-thrash guard so an oscillating workload doesn't re-trace forever; the cheap tier is the per-iteration miss-rate/divergence counters, the expensive tier is the trace+recalibrate.

sources.title: Runtime profiling in OpenJDK's HotSpot JVM
sources.claim: HotSpot uses always-on hotness counters; crossing a compile threshold triggers recompilation; deopt+recompile is rate-limited to prevent thrashing.
sources.verifier_note: Cross-domain analogy (canonical JIT behavior); cited from the research agent, not re-fetched this run. Both LLM lenses PLAUSIBLE; well-established. Provides the anti-thrash design pattern.
